doc.title: Chico Freeman interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001

title: How the music business has changed and lost individuality
summary: He feels institutionalization and industry standards push musicians to look backward rather than be original.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: What’s it like for you today? Being successful in the music business, has it changed in the last let’s say ten years?

Yes. Very much. I’m not sure it’s changed for the better. It’s changed. I have questions about it. The institutionalization of the music has been good on one end and I think it’s not good on another end. I think that the industry has standards and the concepts that they project as to what is acceptable in the industry, and it has for the first time gotten musicians feeling that the idea is to look backwards instead of looking forward. And I think music has always looked forward, with respect to its history. But I mean the industry, the idea of being an individual and being original is less strong today than it was in the past I think.
And you think that the record companies don’t encourage the individuality.
